transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Ava M (Redwood AE), Jonah P (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz, Marcus Hale, Priya Nair, Samuel Reed (sec)
Shared artifacts: Scorecard v1.8 spreadsheet (drive.link/scorecard-v1-8), Guardrail logs export (drive.link/guard-logs), Pricing draft (link/pilot-pricing)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in focusing on quality metrics and two regression clusters that cropped up after last model tweak. Discussed guardrail thresholds, false positive patterns, and a fallback strategy to keep production stable.

[00:00] Ava: ok hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick roll call, um Jonah you're on?
[00:07] Jonah: yea here, Jonah Patel from Redwood SE. i ran the new scoring sweep last night and have some slides, or uh spreadsheet results in the drive.
[00:16] Dr. Lena: Lena here, sorry caught a flight but i am on. we've got Priya and Marcus with me.
[00:22] Priya: hey all.
[00:24] Marcus: morning, Marcus.
[00:26] Samuel: Samuel, security. i'll mostly listen but chime on retention.
[00:31] Ava: great. quick agenda: scorecard review, two regression clusters, guardrail tuning, security asks, next steps. if anything missing add now.
[00:40] Priya: sounds good. also we want to confirm the fall back plan — if the model starts drifting during canary.

--- Scorecard review ---
[01:05] Jonah: alright um pulling up scorecard v1.8. week over week overall accuracy on the classification task is 89.4% down from 92.1 last week, the primary delta corresponds to cluster B — which are these rare radiology phrasing examples, right?
[01:25] Dr. Lena: yeah those are the ones. many of them have shorthand and units, and the model is truncating or guessing units.
[01:32] Marcus: to clarify — these are prompts coming from our legacy ingestion system that strips some of the metadata. so some prompts look like 'CXR AP 4cm nodule, compare 2019' and lack context.
[01:45] Jonah: right, that stripped context is both a prompt engineering issue and a model generalization issue. in the spreadsheet i marked examples where the KB cache — the K V cache — like our prefix cache isn't helping because the prompt lacks a patient context token.
[02:00] Ava: is that something we can fix with prompt templates or do we need to bump model variant?
[02:06] Jonah: short: both. templating will recover maybe half the cases; switching to the q4_8bit quantized variant gives a marginal improvement in recall on these short, structured radiology lines. but it's also slightly higher latency.
[02:18] Dr. Lena: latency thresholds for us are soft — we care more about correctness, but we cannot exceed 1.2s p95 on our UI lookup path.
[02:28] Jonas: (laughs) sorry, jonah.
[02:30] Jonah: noted. i did a small latency run — locally, end-to-end with prefix cache warm — the q4_8bit p95 was 1.0s on the dedicated machine we used, with batch size 1 and continuous batching disabled. in production i expect some variance, so SE suggests we run a 2k-sample in the infra to be safe.

--- Regression clusters ---
[03:05] Jonah: cluster A is hallucination on medication names — those showed up after we applied the paraphrase-oriented prompt augmentation last Friday. cluster B is the radiology shorthand issue.
[03:18] Priya: for cluster A, can we tune the guardrail to be more conservative on medication entities? it's causing false positives in denials.
[03:27] Jonah: yes, we can tune the NER threshold and drop any low-confidence extraction. right now our guardrails are using a token-level threshold of 0.65 which we can bump to 0.75 for medication spans; that'll reduce false positives but might drop some true positives.
[03:41] Dr. Lena: what's the tradeoff numerically?
[03:44] Jonah: in the test set, raising to 0.75 dropped medication recall from 0.88 to 0.80 but precision improved from 0.72 to 0.87, net F1 change was -0.01 so it's marginal.
[03:56] Marcus: given patient safety concerns, i think Priya and i prefer higher precision — fewer false alerts.
[04:01] Priya: agreed. we'll accept lower recall if it means fewer false denials to clinicians.

--- Guardrail false positives pattern ---
[04:15] Jonah: looking through the logs (see guard-logs link) a lot of the false positives are short prompts that match medication patterns due to punctuation. example: 'aspirin 81 mg / daily' sometimes the parser treats '81 mg / daily' as two entities.
[04:32] Dr. Lena: could be a tokenization difference. our ingest pipeline normalizes slashes into spaces — maybe that's changing the model's view.
[04:38] Jonah: yep, tokenization mismatch is a usual suspect. we can add a pre-normalizer step in the prompt pipeline to standardize units and punctuation. that should reduce those false positives without changing model weights.
[04:51] Ava: ok let's prioritize the pre-normalizer + bump NER threshold for meds.

--- Prompt set augmentation ---
[05:10] Priya: we added 60 new edge-case prompts last sprint; we will upload another 200 by end of week. many are client-sourced.
[05:18] Jonah: great — if you can label expected output (even rough), we can compute precision/recall against the scorecard automatically.
[05:25] Priya: yes we'll do labels as: accept / escalate / ignore.
[05:28] Dr. Lena: one ask — can Redwood's scoring support weighted errors? some mistakes are more severe (e.g., medication hallucination) and we want to weight those higher.
[05:38] Jonah: current scorecard supports custom weights; i can add a column 'severity_weight' and rerun the metrics. that'll change the overall 'quality index' number you see.
[05:46] Marcus: good, we want severity_weight 3 for medication halluc, 2 for diagnostic misreads, 1 for small formatting issues.

--- Security & deployment questions ---
[06:05] Samuel: quick security notes: retention window for logs in the current hosted pilot is 30 days. for Private or VPC pilot we need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS for key rotation.
[06:18] Ava: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; Jonah can share docs.
[06:25] Jonah: i'll pull the KMS integration spec and the SOC2 artifact pack. also note that audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via S3 or direct syslog.
[06:36] Dr. Lena: perfect. also we need to know data residency — some records must remain in EU region. can we pin model serving region?
[06:45] Jonah: yes, routing policy supports region pinning per-customer; we'll configure that in the Dedicated setup for Praxis.

--- Fallback / rollout policy ---
[07:02] Ava: Priya asked about fallback — you want canary or immediate fallback?
[07:07] Priya: prefer canary with a fast rollback if quality drops. we want ability to fallback to a smaller conservative model or a rule-based path.
[07:15] Jonah: recommended pattern: canary at 5% traffic to q4_8bit, monitor the weighted quality index and latency p95 for 30 minutes; if weighted quality index drops >3 points or p95 exceeds 1.4s then automatic rollback. we can also route fallback to a rule-based responder for critical medication detection.
[07:34] Marcus: and can we fake-run a rollback drill? like simulate a regression and test the automation?
[07:39] Jonah: yes we can do a rollback dry-run in staging — it will exercise the policy. i'll add that as an action item.

--- Triage of two specific examples ---
[08:05] Jonah: reading example 114 in the sheet: 'CXR AP 4cm nodule compare 2019' model returned 'no acute cardiopulmonary disease' — that's clearly wrong. i marked steps: add template 'include prior studies context token' and add prompt exemplar 114a.
[08:24] Dr. Lena: we'll push that exemplar. Marcus can add the context token at ingestion.
[08:29] Marcus: yes we can modify ingestion, timeline a two-day sprint.
[08:32] Priya: question: if we modify ingestion, does that change our evaluation baseline?
[08:36] Jonah: it'll change the distribution; we should run the recalibrated scorecard after ingestion changes and before a canary.

--- Pricing and pilot terms ---
[09:12] Ava: quick commercial note — i'll send the updated pricing sheet. Praxis asked about burst capacity for a big evening batch job. we offered dedicated burst add-on at 2x baseline for 3 hours.
[09:26] Marcus: sounds ok, need to see numbers.
[09:29] Ava: i'll include cost examples and a monthly committed tier.

--- Recap & next steps ---
[10:00] Ava: recap: Jonah will run the 2k latency baseline on q4_8bit and share CSV; Jonah will also add severity_weight support and document rollback dry-run. Priya/Marcus will upload 200 edge prompts and add labels. Ava will send pricing and pilot terms. Security — schedule deep-dive for 3/19.
[10:22] Dr. Lena: thanks, and please highlight any changes that might affect our scoring baseline.
[10:28] Jonah: will do.
[10:31] Priya: one last thing — can we get a small sample of per-token cost projection for q4_8bit vs current? just a ballpark.
[10:39] Ava: yes, i'll include that in the pricing email.
[10:42] Samuel: retention question — if we go Private can logs be retained longer than 30 days?
[10:46] Jonah: yes, retention is configurable in Private; by default it's customer-managed.
[10:50] Marcus: perfect.
[10:52] Ava: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items. end call.
